nodes.text: Diverse TinyML hardware and software stacks make fair, reproducible comparison of accuracy, latency and energy hard.
nodes.audience_note: reader must know what a microcontroller and on-device inference are

nodes.text: The authors say comparison is needed for progress: optimizations across the stack are hard to measure without it.
CoreMark, MLMark and the MLPerf inference benchmark exist, as characterized by the authors.
None of these gives small ML benchmarks for microcontroller-class devices with power measurement (authors' characterization).
RQ1: which tasks, models and quality targets define a representative, fitting benchmark?
RQ2: which rules and measurement procedure allow fair comparison and still show different contributions?
RQ3: does the v0.5 submission round show the benchmark accommodating diverse submitters?
Four benchmarks with reference implementations, quality targets, closed and open divisions and a measurement framework.
Choice of four tasks, datasets, models and quality targets, with reference accuracies.
Closed/open divisions, modular reference implementation, measurement procedure and framework.
First submission round (June 2021), peer-reviewed by submitters and a review committee.
Reference models reach or exceed the quality targets: VWW about 86% vs 80%, IC 86.5% vs 85%, KWS 91.6% vs 90%, AD AUC 0.88/0.86 vs 0.85.
Authors state each reference implementation meets the minimum accuracy and covers a wide scope in latency and energy (values not available).
Five Table 2 rows: four closed (ARM MCU, RISC-V MCU, LEIP on RasPi 4, Syntiant accelerator) and one open FPGA; trends and no dataset modified.
The chosen tasks and targets give an accuracy floor while allowing for quantization differences.
The authors attribute fair yet flexible comparison to the modular, two-division design and measurement framework.
The authors read the diverse round as evidence that the modular design accommodates different goals.
An open-source, four-benchmark suite measuring accuracy, latency and energy with reference implementations, divisions and a framework.
Streaming and pre-processing limits (author-stated).
Long-term stability and model-family coverage (author-stated).
Writer-derived: no variance, no figure values, one round, no submission measurements.
The authors expect standardization and responsible-deployment standards, and name misuse and e-waste risks.
New domains, stable subset, pre-processing scope, RNNs.
Quantization (PTQ, QAT, INT-8) and the quality metrics Top-1 and AUC-ROC.
Device under test, inferences per second, micro-Joules per inference.

experiment_chains.experiment: Reference models evaluated against candidate quality targets (four tasks)
experiment_chains.hypothesis: Objective (writer's framing of the authors' aim): set quality targets so a correct quantized implementation passes, using measured reference accuracies.
experiment_chains.falsifier: A reference model falling below its target (none reported).
experiment_chains.design_rationale: Targets set slightly below reference accuracy to accommodate quantization and rounding (C029).
experiment_chains.next: Reference targets fix accuracy; the next question is how latency and energy are measured on the reference platform.

experiment_chains.experiment: Reference implementations on NUCLEO-L4R5ZI (latency, energy, accuracy)
experiment_chains.hypothesis: Objective: show that the four references run under the framework and meet minimum accuracy.
experiment_chains.falsifier: A reference failing its minimum accuracy (none reported).
experiment_chains.design_rationale: Reference platform and known-good TFLM snapshot for stability (C034).
experiment_chains.next: With references fixed, the question is whether outside submitters can use the suite in different ways.

experiment_chains.hypothesis: Objective: show the benchmark can accommodate submissions from hardware and software vendors in both divisions.
experiment_chains.falsifier: Only one kind of submitter or division taking part (not the case in Table 2).
experiment_chains.design_rationale: Modular design and two divisions (C027, C028).
experiment_chains.next: The round is a snapshot; later rounds are expected to show evolution (C022).
